summary: Pipeline order is normative: includes inline before parsing (a .md page converts first, then inlines — §10.1); layouts before URL phases; §11.1→§11.2→§11.3; collisions before write; reference check on temp tree; publish last
Best-effort composition: a problem in one page never stops analysis of others; all problems in the site reported in one pass
Preservation: all bytes outside an edited span are preserved exactly; the layout's text is the base document
Include splice: the include element or SSI comment is replaced by the included file's processed contents
Slot fill: the slot element is replaced by the fill elements in page order; the consumed slot attribute is removed; nothing else about a fill's markup changes
Slot fallback: slot start/end tags removed, inner bytes kept as written
Children replacement: the element's children are replaced by the default content; the element itself, tag and attributes, stays
Unwrap: page's first <main> start tag and matching end tag deleted; inner bytes stay in place
Removal: removed elements are removed entirely; removed attributes (data-layout, consumed slot) are removed cleanly; removal changes nothing else
Head replacement in place: the page's element(s) take the layout element's position in page order; other same-key layout elements removed per S07
Head append: appended head elements land at the end of the layout's head content, in page-source order
Title join: layout title inner text becomes pageText + " " + layoutText, both trimmed; layout's title tag kept
Root attributes: class = layout tokens then page tokens not already present; overridden attr edited in place; new attr inserted before closing > in page order
Default content: nodes kept in source order with interior text preserved as written; boundary whitespace-only text nodes are not significant
Output shell (doctype, html, head, body tags) is the layout's; page's doctype/shell not emitted; page with no layout emitted from its own text (layout-less .md: converted body inside the §10.7 shell)
--exclude repeatable; unify.yaml key exclude is a list; default is the single glob _*; user globs replace the default
Pattern without / tested against every path segment of the source-root-relative path
Pattern with / tested against the full source-root-relative path with * ** ? […] semantics
A matched directory segment excludes the entire subtree; files inside a _-directory need no own underscore
Excluded files are never emitted but remain build material: includable and usable as layouts
Underscore guard: an emitted _-prefixed page or a path containing a _-prefixed directory segment is a problem naming the file and the fixing --exclude line
The guard does not cover _-prefixed non-page files; the exclude-replacement recipe ships _headers/_redirects cleanly
Never-shipped list exactly: output dir inside root, .git/.hg/.svn, node_modules, .env and .env.*, unify.yaml; not replaceable; never scanned; dotfiles ship
Mirror copy: every emitted asset copied byte-for-byte to the same source-root-relative path
Symlinks followed only while resolving inside the source root; outside → treated as absent with advisory A12

Defaulted-source notice: when the source root defaulted to the working directory (no --source flag, no unify.yaml source key, no src/), the stdout summary reports the copied-file count and points at --dry-run; explicit --source (even .) or an existing src/ suppresses it; never a diagnostic, never affects exit

Fragments: a name ending .fragment.html is not a page - mirror-copied byte-for-byte, never composed or rewritten, never moved by --pretty-urls, insides not reference-checked (runtime resolution base is the consuming page), still an ordinary include target; references to it are checked and rewritten normally; underscore still excludes it
SSI virtual="P" resolves against the source root; leading / permitted and equivalent
SSI file="P" must be relative and resolves against dirname of the including file
<include src="P">: leading / resolves from source root, else relative to the including file
Resolved include path escaping the source root is a problem (not-found shape); traversal safety internal and always on
Include target must exist and end .html/.md; otherwise a located problem with fix lines including spelling-and-casing
A .md include target is converted first (frontmatter stripped and ignored, heading ids applied); .html used verbatim
Include targets' own includes process recursively before splicing
Include cycle detection by resolved-path stack; depth cap 10 inclusive (a chain ten deep builds, the include pushing an eleventh is the problem); both problems print the full chain
<include> without src is a problem
<include> with non-whitespace content between its tags is a problem; includes never take fills
Void <include> builds identically and carries advisory A01

Inlining is textual and pre-parse for HTML hosts (in Markdown: post-conversion, §10.1 — timing is the only difference): includes work anywhere (head, Markdown); fragment top-level elements become the host's (may carry slot= fills or contribute <slot> elements)
Layout selection order, first match wins: data-layout=none / frontmatter layout:none; data-layout=V; frontmatter layout:V; nearest _layout.html walking up; else none
Discovery walk is by file name; the layout file's excluded status is irrelevant
Explicit layout value not ending .html (bare name) is a problem before any existence check
Layout path resolution: / from source root, else relative to the declaring file
Layout target missing or escaping the source root is a problem with the include-not-found shape including the casing fix line
data-layout on a non-root element is a problem naming <include src> as the replacement
Any data-unify attribute anywhere in any source file — excluded files included; only the never-shipped list escapes scanning — is a problem naming the v0.7.0 spelling
Any class token beginning unify- anywhere in any source file (excluded files included) is a problem naming the slot spelling
data-layout never appears in output (removed per S07, including the none form)
A <script> carrying data-polyfill is removed entirely from built output
A layout that itself declares data-layout (any value, including none) is a problem P15 - layout chaining is not supported in v0.7.0; never a silent no-op
Sinks are the <slot> elements in the layout's <body> (skipping any inside <template>) plus the layout's first <main>; neither → sink-less
First bare <slot> is the default slot; further bare slots get advisory A13 (duplicated construct) and render their fallback
First <slot name=X> per X receives X's fills; a repeated name gets advisory A13 and later ones render their fallback
A <slot> outside a layout's <body> (in any page, or a layout's <head>) is problem P20 and is replaced by its own children
Duplicate <main> in a layout: the first wins, advisory A13

When the layout has at least one sink, the page's first <main> — in document order, at any depth, not only top level — is unwrapped once (S06); a <main> inside the first survives; no other element is unwrapped

Fills are the direct element children of the page body and of the page's first <main> wherever it sat, carrying a non-empty slot attribute; slot="" counts as absent; slot anywhere else is never touched or reported
Default content is everything else in the page body - elements, text, comments - in source order (S12)
For each name with fills, <slot name> is replaced by the fills in page order (S03)
A fill naming a slot the layout lacks: advisory A02, slot attribute consumed, element stays in place in the default-content sequence
Each unfilled named slot is replaced by its own children (S04); fallback content is plain markup (a nested slot is P16/MRG-19); slots inside <template> ship as written
Default slot present → default content replaces it; empty default content → the default slot renders its fallback
No default slot, layout has <main> → default content replaces <main>'s children (S05); empty default content → <main> keeps its children
No default slot, no <main>, named slots exist, default content non-empty → problem (content would vanish)
Every message about a slot or a layout names the layout file it was checked against
Sink-less layout: whole <body> is the default slot; page body children replace layout body children verbatim (S05, no unwrap); head-only layout is legitimate
A <header>/<footer> that is not a fill is default content: it ships in place and is not reported (A03 retired)

The content-loss law: authored content is never dropped without failing the build; every rule places content or raises a problem (enforced across all fixtures via diagnosticsExhaustive + tree assertions)
Slots do not nest: a <slot> inside another slot's fallback content is a problem P16 - fallback content is plain markup

The merge requires a <body> on both sides: a missing one is P21 at the file that lacks it and the page is not built; an empty resolved layout file is this problem, never a silent no-layout; a body-less layout never publishes its own text as the page
Charset: page's dropped in favor of layout's which stays first; layout without one -> page's kept and moved first; identical silent; different -> advisory A08
Title joined per S10 in the layout title's position; empty/whitespace page title counts as absent; layout without <title> → page's title appends with its own text

Meta name/property keyed ASCII case-insensitively: replaces in place (S08); multiple page elements with one key all kept; dedup only crosses the layout/page boundary; no layout counterpart → appends (fixture M1); http-equiv not keyed → appends
link rel=canonical replaces in place; one canonical, never two
link with icon in its rel token list (covers shortcut icon, ASCII case-insensitive): all layout icon links removed, page set takes the first one's position; apple-touch-icon not keyed
Stylesheet/script-src dedup by URL compared after §11.1 resolution — page copy dropped, layout position stands; inline script/style with byte-identical content: page copy dropped
Everything else appends after the layout's head content in page-source order (S09); page CSS loads last
On html/body only: page class tokens appended to the layout's without repeats
Any other attribute the page sets wins: edited in place if the layout had it, inserted before > otherwise
data-layout and consumed slot attributes are removed before the root-attribute merge; a page cannot remove a layout attribute; attributes merge nowhere else
CommonMark, no extensions beyond §10.4 heading ids; output filename swaps .md for .html

Include timing in Markdown: conversion first — include tags/SSI comments pass through the converter as raw HTML and resolve on the converted output; fragment contents are spliced verbatim, never converted; a .md include target converts exactly once
Layout rules apply exactly as for an HTML page whose body is the converted output and whose head is synthesized from frontmatter
Frontmatter is YAML between --- fences at the very start of the file
title key becomes the page's <title>, then merges per §8 row 2
layout key drives layout selection per §6.1
class key adds class tokens to the page's <body>
lang and dir keys set those attributes on <html>
Any other scalar key becomes <meta name="KEY" content="VALUE">
og: block entries become <meta property="og:K" content="V">
Any other block (twitter: …) entries become <meta name="BLOCK:K" content="V">
A list value emits one <meta> per item, in order
Synthesized elements merge per §8 as if page-written; serialization fixed: double-quoted attributes, name/property before content, <title>TEXT</title>
No other reserved keys: date/tags/categories/draft/permalink/slug become plain metas; draft:true publishes; a leading underscore holds a page back
No frontmatter title → text of the first <h1> in the converted body with inline markup stripped; neither → no page title, the layout's stands alone
Heading id algorithm: lowercase, whitespace runs to single hyphens, drop non-letter/digit/hyphen (Unicode kept), trim hyphens, -2/-3 on repeats; explicit id kept; HTML pages never touched
Frontmatter fence at byte 0 of an .html page is a problem
A literal <head> element in a Markdown body is a problem

The include-block extension: a line beginning <include starts an HTML block (as if include were on CommonMark's type-6 list); line-initial include/SSI splices as a block, in-paragraph include splices inline; include syntax in a code fence or code span is escaped text, never a directive

Layout-less .md emits inside the minimal synthesized shell: doctype; <html> with frontmatter lang/dir; <head> with charset first, then title when one exists, then metas in source order; <body> with frontmatter class holding the converted body; nothing else synthesized

Value serialization: plain scalars as source text (true, 2026-01-01, 0.50 as written — no YAML coercion); quoted scalars unquoted; block scalars as YAML defines; empty value → empty string; lists compose with blocks (one meta per item)
Provenance rewriting applies to every URL in href, src, srcset (each URL, descriptors untouched), poster — after includes and layouts, before §11.2/§11.3
Skipped: scheme or // prefix, mailto/tel/data/javascript, fragment-only, empty values
Never reached: url() inside <style> blocks or style attributes — write those root-relative or in stylesheet files
A URL starting with / is unchanged by §11.1
A relative URL whose provenance is a layout or include file resolves against that file's directory and is emitted root-relative
A relative URL whose provenance is the page stays exactly as written — unless the page's output moved (--pretty-urls), then resolved and emitted root-relative
Pretty files: every page output X.html moves to X/index.html except any index.html and the root 404.html
Pretty links: after §11.1, every internal URL resolving to an emitted page's .html output is rewritten resolve-first then transformed, emitted root-relative (the eight-row table)
Pretty preserves untouched: external URLs, mailto/tel/data, fragment-only, URLs to non-page files; query and fragment always survive

base-url is the whole address (scheme+domain); a bare path is a usage error, exit 2. Its path part prefixes every root-relative URL in href/src/srcset/poster plus root-relative og:/twitter: meta content

base-url origin is prepended to og:/twitter: content and canonical href — absolutization is always origin + path prefix (og:image /assets/x.jpg under https://host/repo/ emits https://host/repo/assets/x.jpg)
base-url leaves non-root-relative values untouched; source files stay rooted at /; order §11.1→§11.2→§11.3

Check scope: every emitted HTML file's href/src/srcset/poster, link href for every rel, root-relative og:/twitter: meta content; url() in emitted CSS files, <style> blocks, and style attributes (rewriting-exempt but checked)

Internal = after stripping the base-url prefix (path prefix, or the full origin+path base when a full URL was given — absolutized values stay checkable), root-relative or relative (resolved against the containing output file's URL); query/fragment stripped; external and mailto/tel/data/fragment-only skipped
A directory URL (trailing / or empty path) checks for index.html within it
A URL resolving to no emitted file is a problem naming the source file, the reference, and the line where known
Case is compared byte-for-byte; a reference matching only case-insensitively fails
#fragment targets are not validated against ids

A reference resolving to the output path of a source page that exists but failed to compose is NOT reported (its own problem already blocks the publish); a target with no source file, and an excluded-but-existing target, still fail
Two sources producing one output path is a problem naming both sources
A --pretty-urls move landing on another source's output is a problem naming both sources
Two outputs differing only by letter case: advisory A11
Pages and assets cannot collide by construction; collisions detected before any write; no last-write-wins anywhere
Two severities only: problem and advisory; never "warning", "error:", or rule codes
Exit 0: published (with --dry-run: would have)
Exit 1: problems found (or advisories under --strict); nothing published; previous output untouched
Exit 2: invalid usage or fatal environment error (unknown flag, missing source dir, --clean containment refusal, port in use)
Diagnostics to stderr; build summary and --dry-run list to stdout; both ordered by path then line; two runs print the same bytes
Every diagnostic line begins FILE:LINE: SEVERITY: (line omitted when unknown); prefix and severity token are stable contract, message prose is not
Continuation lines indented two spaces: in: and fix:; path-shaped messages always include the spelling-and-casing fix line
Cycle and depth messages print the full chain joined with " → "
DEBUG=1 adds stack traces
Advisory discipline: unify init && unify build --dry-run --strict exits 0; an advisory firing on a correct site is a bug in the advisory

Attribution conventions are contract: cycle/depth problems locate at the outermost include site; collision problems at the path-ordered first colliding source; every other located diagnostic — §6 layout selection, §7 composition, §8 charset advisory, §12 references — at the provenance file of the offending markup and its line IN that file, never the host post-inlining line

A line that cannot be mapped to the named file is omitted, not guessed: the FILE: SEVERITY: form is used (a .md page converts before inlining, so an offset attributed to Markdown source indexes converted HTML)

Diagnostics are deduplicated before counting or printing: same file, line, severity, message, in: and fix: lines = one diagnostic; genuinely distinct faults that print identically (a relative url() in shared chrome resolving per consumer) are distinguished by resolved target and both printed
Problem: include target missing, wrong extension, or escaping the source root
Problem: include cycle or depth over 10, chain printed
Problem: <include> without src; <include> with non-whitespace content
Problem: layout reference not a .html path (bare name)
Problem: layout target missing or escaping the source root
Problem: data-layout on a non-root element
Problem: data-unify attribute; unify- class token
Problem: unaddressed page content with no sink in a slotted layout
Problem: frontmatter in an .html page
Problem: literal <head> in a Markdown body
Problem: output collision
Problem: broken internal reference
Problem: emitted _-prefixed page or _-directory path
Problem: a layout declares data-layout - layout chaining is not supported in v0.7.0
Problem: a <slot> nested inside another slot's fallback content - slots do not nest
Problem: a frontmatter value with no text form - a mapping nested below a key that already names one, or a list item that is itself a mapping or list
Problem: frontmatter is not valid YAML - a parse failure, distinct from P17's shape rule
Problem: a named slot inside the layout's default-content sink main, with no bare slot - the two rules target overlapping spans
Problem: <slot> outside a layout's <body> (anywhere in a page, or in a layout's <head>); the fix names the spelling that belongs in that file. Was advisory A04
Problem: a page or layout with no <body> element where a merge requires one; attributed file-level to the file that lacks it, fix spelled for that file's kind
Advisory: void <include> used
Advisory: fill names a slot the layout doesn't have; content stayed in the page flow
Advisory: page charset differs from the layout's, layout's kept
Advisory: working-format file emitted; closed extension list .psd .ai .sketch .fig .xcf
Advisory: a file used as a layout or include also ships as its own page
Advisory: output paths differing only by case
Advisory: symlink resolving outside the source root, treated as absent
Advisory: duplicated construct of which only the first counts - second bare <slot>, repeated slot name, or second <main>; message names the construct

Advisory: known deployment file at the source root held back by the exclude set (maintained list, non-normative; today _headers, _redirects, _routes.json, _worker.js); names the file and the --exclude line that ships it; source-root names only
Transactional publish: zero problems → publish; any problem → previous output byte-for-byte untouched and exit 1
Publish sync: unchanged files not rewritten; files no longer produced deleted; new/changed land via temp-then-rename
--clean empties the output directory first; refuses with exit 2 when the output directory is, or contains, the source root or the working directory - not when it merely sits inside them
--dry-run runs the entire pipeline through the report with no writes at all
Saves coalesce into one rebuild; a save landing mid-rebuild queues exactly one follow-up; no change dropped
Every rebuild is full; watch output after any edit sequence is identical to a fresh unify build
Watch writes are minimal and atomic: unchanged files untouched, temp-then-rename, precise deletions; --clean applies only at startup
While watching, a failing page is emitted as a default error page carrying the located diagnostics, replaced on next success; unify build never emits error pages
unify dev = watch + static server on localhost:port (default 3000) serving the output directory with directory indexes and a 404 page, plus a reload event stream
The reload script is injected only into HTML responses dev serves and never exists in the output directory
No proxying, HTTPS, middleware, or config in dev — permanently (asserted by the closed CLI surface test: unknown flags exit 2)
--dry-run report: stdout, one list ordered by output path, one line per action, verbs write/copy/delete only
Every write line names its inputs: the source page and the layout it resolved to
Under --dry-run, diagnostics print to stderr exactly as a real build would
--dry-run states the address it is building for (base-url, or the domain root when unset), and each write/copy row carries the URL that file answers to
unify.yaml keys are the long option names: source output clean exclude pretty-urls base-url strict port; exclude replaces the default like the flag
CLI flags win over unify.yaml on conflict
No behavior exists that only the file can express; the file itself is never emitted

Every template scaffolds into src/ beside a dist-free root and exercises each primitive exactly once: one include (nav), automatic _layout.html, one named slot with fallback (footer) plus a page filling it, one data-layout=none page (404.html), and _includes/
Scaffolded layout declares <meta charset="utf-8">; a plain HTML comment above each slot; starter stylesheet includes slot { display: contents }; built pages contain no <slot> elements

The blog template ships _scripts/gen.mjs (zero dependencies, opening comment naming the authoring rules' literal node _scripts/gen.mjs && unify build) reading posts/*.md and _data/authors.json and writing blog.html and feed.xml into the source tree, shipped pre-generated: rerunning the script reproduces the checked-in tree byte-for-byte
unify init && unify build --dry-run --strict exits 0 (asserted per template)

The blog generator teaches field privacy: _data/authors.json carries a private email beside public fields; gen.mjs names the fields it emits (never spreads the record), so the email appears in no generated file and nowhere in built output; both generated files carry the "generated by _scripts/gen.mjs — edit the data, not this file" marker
Worked example: nested include with relative resolution, exact
Worked example C1: golden path, <main> default with unwrap, exact
Worked example C2: named slot replaces the element, exact body
Worked example C3: unfilled slot renders its fallback, exact body
Worked example C4: multiple fills one name, in page order
Worked example C5: fill to a nonexistent slot — advisory A02, content preserved
Worked example C6: bare slot inside <main>, pinning by markup
Worked example C8: sink-less head-only passthrough, exact
Worked example C9: slots inside <template> never touched
Worked example: the whole head-merge table at once, exact
Worked example: root-attribute merge one-liner
Worked example: Markdown end to end, exact
Worked example C7: a layout declaring data-layout is a problem P15 (realized as landmine layout-declares-layout)

Membership: one record per composed page, in output-path order; assets, .fragment.html files, excluded sources, and pages that failed to compose have no record; a page with no metadata still gets a complete record

Extraction reads the emitted text only (post-includes, post-Markdown, post-composition, post-§11); layout-supplied metadata is read per shipping page; <template> contents are never scanned; deriving the manifest changes no output, diagnostic, or exit code

Every record carries every field; absent scalars are null and absent lists are []; text content resolves numeric and HTML 4.01 named character references (leaving unknown ones as written), omits script/style/template/noscript subtrees, contributes one space on entering and leaving every non-inline element, collapses whitespace runs to one space, and trims; image width/height are read only when the url came from og:image

Single-valued fields keep the first accepted declaration in document order; differing repeats append one conflicts entry {field, kept, discarded} ordered by field name; identical repeats are not conflicts; a conflict is data, never a §14 diagnostic

path is publish.js's urlForOutputPath (index.html dropped, --base-url path prefix applied) with every output-path segment percent-encoded and the base-url prefix left alone; url is origin+path with --base-url and null without it

robots parsed from <meta name="robots"> only: comma-split lowercased directives, indexable false on noindex/none, followable false on nofollow/none; googlebot meta and robots.txt are never read into a record
text is the text content of the first <main>, else <body>, else the whole document

jsonLd is one {raw, data, error} per ld+json script in document order, parsing never throws; schemaType is the first of <meta name="schema"> or a single-object string @type, and arrays/@graph/missing/non-string @type declare nothing

linksOut holds deduplicated sorted output paths of linked pages that have records, after base-url stripping, with query/fragment discarded and skipped-URL schemes excluded; linksIn is its exact reverse

Activation is --base-url and governs the whole section, §21.6 included: without it no sitemap is emitted, an authored one is an ordinary mirror-copied asset, and nothing about sitemaps is reported; generation is additive, appears in --dry-run, and participates in transactional publish

Membership is the closed list: has a record, robots.indexable, output path is not 404.html, and self-canonical (no canonical, or one resolving to its own output path via §12's resolution); entries appear in manifest order

Each entry is <loc> = record.url, percent-encoded by §20.5 and then XML-escaped, plus <lastmod> only when dateModified.iso is non-null; never the build clock, filesystem time, filename, Git history, or datePublished; no changefreq and no priority

urlset in the sitemaps 0.9 namespace, UTF-8, newline-terminated, byte-identical across runs; over 50,000 URLs or 50 MiB the output is a sitemap index at sitemap.xml naming sitemap-1.xml, sitemap-2.xml, filled in manifest order
An authored sitemap.xml suppresses generation entirely and ships byte-for-byte; a generated path occupied by an emitted source file is P22 located at that file, with generation suppressed

Every internal <loc> in an emitted output-root sitemap, generated or authored, must resolve to an emitted file or raise P13 located at the sitemap; other-origin values are skipped rather than fetched; the document is parsed, so a <loc> in a comment declares nothing, a CDATA-wrapped value is the value, and a namespace-prefixed loc is a loc
Generated discovery artifact's output path already occupied by a file emitted from source; located at the occupying source file; generation suppressed rather than overwriting

iso is the declared value only when it is well-formed W3C-DTF (literal T, TZD required with a time, real calendar day, real time of day, offset within ±14:00), verbatim rather than normalized, else null; raw always keeps the author's bytes and is never emitted; no date is ever derived from the clock, filesystem, filename, or Git history
